articles.title: Environmental poliovirus detection declines across Pakistan, positivity falls to 13.1pc
articles.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has recorded a significant decline in the detection of poliovirus in environmental samples during the first six months of 2026, with the positivity rate dropping from 48.1 per cent during the same period last year to 13.1pc this year. Prime Minister’s Focal Person for Polio Eradication Ayesha Raza Farooq told Dawn that the improvement was the result of a new strategy involving external audits, better team selection, enhanced training and the support of law enforcement agencies. However, a polio expert cautioned that unchecked cross-border movement from Afghanistan remained a major concern, as poliovirus strains linked to Kandahar and Nangarhar had been detected in environmental samples collected from Quetta and Peshawar, respectively. According to data released by the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication, 127 environmental samples were collected across the country during June 2026 as part of routine poliovirus surveillance. Of these, 117 tested negative, while 10 samples were confirmed positive. The number of positive environmental samples detected between January and June also declined significantly, falling from 369 during the same period in 2025 to 100 this year. According to the NEOC, Punjab reported no positive environmental samples, with all 31 samples collected during June testing negative for poliovirus. In Sindh, 28 of the 29 samples tested negative, while one sample was positive. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa recorded 30 negative samples out of 34, whereas Balochistan reported 18 negative samples out of 23. The NEOC said the decline in environmental positivity reflected improvements in vaccination coverage and surveillance efforts, but stressed that sustained vigilance was essential to interrupt virus transmission. Pakistan has reported three wild poliovirus cases so far this year, with the NEOC intensifying surveillance and vaccination efforts in high-risk areas. It urged community leaders, religious scholars and healthcare professionals to support polio eradication efforts and appealed to the public to facilitate polio workers. Environmental surveillance is considered one of the key indicators of the effectiveness of polio vaccination campaigns. The detection of poliovirus in sewage samples indicates continued virus circulation and highlights gaps in immunisation coverage. While polio cases may emerge in different areas due to population movement, the presence of the virus in environmental samples points to shortcomings in vaccination efforts within those communities. Responding to a question, Farooq said the main challenges persisted in southern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Karachi. “We decided to conduct an external audit in Karachi, and based on its findings, new vaccination teams were selected and trained. We received full cooperation from the chief secretary of Sindh, which helped reduce the number of positive environmental samples to just one in the province during June. Karachi is densely populated, and routine immunisation coverage is also not satisfactory, so it requires continued attention,” she said. Regarding Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, she said access remained a major challenge. “We have involved law enforcement agencies as well as local communities. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is personally taking interest, and the entire team is committed to addressing the issue,” Farooq said. However, a polio expert, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the unchecked movement of people across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border remained the biggest challenge.

articles.title: Kids’ Fruit Pouches Recalled Nationwide Over Contamination Risk
articles.description: Pumpkin Tree Snacks Parents are being urged to check their pantries after a nationwide recall of select Pumpkin Tree Peter Rabbit Organics Banana & Strawberry fruit purée pouches over concerns they could contain plastic. PT Organics voluntarily recalled its 4-ounce pouches after discovering an internal packaging defect could cause a strand of the pouch’s inner material to detach and mix with the fruit purée. The company said the issue is limited to the packaging and does not involve the purée itself. No injuries have been reported, and no other Pumpkin Tree products or flavors are included in the recall. The company said customers should not consume the recalled pouches or feed them to children. “Consumers or caregivers who have recalled product in their possession should dispose of it or return the product to the place of purchase,” the company said. “It should not be eaten or fed to another person.” PT Organics described the recall as the first incident of its kind in the company’s 20 years of business. The affected pouches were sold exclusively at Target, Kroger, and Meijer stores nationwide between March 6 and July 13. Consumers can identify recalled products by checking for barcode 8 15367 01078 0, lane number 4, with best-before dates of Jan. 19, Jan. 20, March 17, March 18, May 14, or May 15, 2027. Read it at People Read more at The Daily Beast.

articles.title: IFRC: One month after Venezuela's earthquakes, health care, psychosocial support and safe water remain urgent priorities
articles.description: Country: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Caracas, Panama City, Geneva 23 July 2026 — One month after the two earthquakes that struck north-central Venezuela, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) and the Venezuelan Red Cross (VRC) have identified three critical areas for humanitarian assistance in the short and medium term: primary health care, mental health care and access to safe drinking water. The IFRC and the VRC are now focusing their efforts on distributing humanitarian aid, delivering health services and carrying out further needs assessments. Their findings show that many families still depend on bottled water to drink, wash and cook. Access to sanitation also remains limited, raising the risk of disease outbreaks in the areas where displaced people are staying. Thousands of people with chronic conditions have yet to fully regain continuity of treatment — an interruption that threatens their wellbeing and can add further strain to the health system. Survivors are also living with anxiety, fear, sadness and sleeplessness as they grieve the loss of loved ones, of their jobs and of their livelihoods. "One month on from the devastating earthquakes that shook our country, we reaffirm our commitment to the Venezuelan people. We have activated every cooperation mechanism of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement to strengthen and complement our response, and we will remain here for those who need it most," said Luis Manuel Farías Villanueva, President of the Venezuelan Red Cross. "We are planning a 24-month operation to keep standing with people; needs have been changing, and our response has adjusted to serve more people and to serve them better." From the very first minute, local Red Cross teams have been alongside the people affected: first setting up a field hospital, supporting the rescue of survivors and reconnecting families who had lost track of their loved ones; and now, distributing humanitarian aid and strengthening primary health care through an emergency clinic in La Guaira. The clinic, set up by the IFRC and managed by the Spanish Red Cross, reinforces the Venezuelan Red Cross field hospital. It will operate for four months and is already delivering health and psychosocial services that will benefit close to 30,000 people. One of them is Gabriel Cipriani, who lost close relatives when his building collapsed and lives with a neurological condition that requires constant medication. For him, the Red Cross remaining there is the difference between continuing his treatment and having it interrupted: "Knowing I can count on a Red Cross doctor made me feel that I am not alone, that there is a hand with me. That gives you security, it gives you confidence." In the coming weeks and months, the priority for the IFRC and the VRC will be to sustain that health care and expand access to safe water while laying the foundations for recovery: strengthening epidemiological surveillance to prevent outbreaks, maintaining psychosocial support and treatment for chronic conditions, and beginning to accompany families as they rebuild their livelihoods. Assistance will be adjusted as needs change, with particular attention to those at greatest risk: children, older people, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and people with chronic illnesses or disabilities. "This disaster is far from over. Continuing to distribute essential items and safeguarding people's wellbeing and public health is, and will remain, a priority in the medium term — but further ahead it will also mean making sure people recover their livelihoods and their income-generating activities," said Loyce Pace, IFRC Regional Director for the Americas*. "A disaster like this one calls for assistance that is multisectoral, comprehensive and sustained over time. The IFRC is committed to the Venezuelan Red Cross and to the people of Venezuela in making that possible — and that is why we are calling for sustained, flexible funding, able to accompany families throughout their recovery."* That funding has a concrete figure. The IFRC launched an Emergency Appeal to raise 50 million Swiss francs to assist 300,000 people over two years. One month on from the disaster, it is 25.19 per cent funded. As people's needs evolve and grow more complex, the resources to meet them should grow at the same pace. Moon Alert

A positive day

Today, Mercury stops being retrograde, which will help you get more organized at home. Nevertheless, opportunities for vacations, sports events and fun socializing with others continue to come your way. At work, co-workers are supportive. It’s all good.

A positive day

Be aware of the limitations of the moon alert today and agree to nothing important. Meanwhile, good news! Today Mercury stops being retrograde, which will reduce transportation delays, car problems and mixed-up communications that you've been dealing with for a while. Brighter skies ahead!

An average day

With fiery Mars in your sign now, you have a lot of energy and drive. However, be aware of the limitations of today's moon alert. (See above.) You'll be happy to know that Mercury stops being retrograde today, which will improve your finances, especially in terms of delays and mistakes.

A positive day

Excellent news! Mercury has been retrograding in your sign since June 29. Today this is over, which means your life will resume a greater degree of normalcy, and silly mistakes will be reduced along with delays and transportation problems. Thank goodness!

Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)

A positive day

Be aware of today's moon alert. Fortunately, you are in a strong position because both the sun and lucky Jupiter are in your sign. Fiery Mars is also well-placed, promoting teamwork, competitive sports and athletics. Starting today, life takes on a forward momentum.

Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)

A positive day

With Venus in your sign, you're enjoying socializing with others. Nevertheless, you also have a strong tendency now to work alone or behind the scenes. You're also ambitious to achieve. With this in mind, be aware that there is a moon alert today. Volunteer for nothing.

Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)

An average day

For the last month, Mercury has been retrograding at the top of your chart, affecting your relations with bosses, parents and authority figures from the past. As of today, this is over. Although you might be focused on financial matters, restrict spending to food and gas.

Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)

A positive day

Today the moon is in your sign, which gives you a slight advantage over the other signs. However, most of this day is a moon alert! (See above.) Therefore, tread carefully and restrict your spending to food and gas. Don't volunteer for anything. Postpone important decisions.

Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)

An average day

It's encouraging that Mercury retrograde is over today because it might have delayed financial matters for you, especially dealing with third parties, partners or the government. Go forward with confidence now to make plans for travel, publishing, medicine, the law and higher education. (Whew!)

Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)

A positive day

In the last month, Mercury has been retrograding opposite your sign, attracting ex-partners and old friends back into your world. (This might have been a mixed blessing for some.) At any rate, as of today, Mercury retrograde is finished. However, check the Moon Alert above!

Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)

A positive day

You'll be relieved to know that today Mercury retrograde stops, as it has been creating equipment problems, delays, and confusion with respect to your job, your health, and even perhaps dealing with your pet. This means your efforts to work will be more efficient and reliable. Yay! (Check moon alert.)

Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)

An average day

Today you might feel restless for adventure or a change. You're working hard, but you also want to explore something new. Fortunately, Mercury stops being retrograde today. Nevertheless, most of this day is a moon alert, so just bide your time. It's all systems go tomorrow!

articles.title: Besieged by lobbyists, will UK ministers protect our ecosystems? No, they’ll chicken out | George Monbiot
articles.description: Industrial poultry farming is killing our rivers. But rather than stop it, the government has been facilitating it. Will Andy Burnham end this ecocide? There’s a slightly mean question I often ask British people with an interest in the living world: can you name the environment secretary? I don’t intend to show them up: it’s not them I’m testing. I watch the brows knit, a finger go up, the mouth open and close. “It’s, you know, the one who ... no, they went, didn’t they? That other one ...” It’s been like this for seven years. Why? Because throughout this period, we’ve not had environment secretaries. We’ve had portals through which corporate lobbyists may pass. The last incumbent to represent the wider public interest (and I can scarcely bring myself to type these words) was Michael Gove. In his other roles, he’s widely remembered with loathing and disgust. Out of office, he continues to poison public life , as editor of the Spectator. But in this role, to general astonishment, he placed the public good above special interests. George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...
